region: Capital city of Bosnia and Herzegovina
heroText: Sarajevo is a mountain-ringed capital where Ottoman lanes, Austro-Hungarian facades and 20th-century history meet in a compact valley. Begin in Bascarsija, cross the Latin Bridge, then ride up to the Yellow Fortress for sunset over the city. Sarajevo International Airport is close, but valley traffic can still shape transfer times.

areas.name: Bascarsija
areas.text: Bascarsija is the old bazaar core, best for first stays focused on cafes, mosques, craft lanes and short walks.

areas.name: Ferhadija
areas.text: Ferhadija keeps you on the pedestrian spine between Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian Sarajevo, with shops and central hotels.

areas.name: Marijin Dvor
areas.text: Marijin Dvor is practical for business hotels, museums, malls and access toward the airport side of the city.

areas.name: Ilidza
areas.text: Ilidza sits near the airport and Vrelo Bosne, useful for spa hotels, green space and early flights.

airports.name: Sarajevo International Airport (SJJ)
airports.search: Sarajevo International Airport, Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina
airports.text: Sarajevo International Airport is southwest of the centre near Ilidza; taxis and transfers are the most common visitor options.

airportTransfer.value: 20-35 min by taxi or transfer to the old town

stayOverview: Bascarsija is the atmospheric first-choice base, Ferhadija works for central walks, Marijin Dvor suits business and museums, and Ilidza is better for airport access, spa hotels and Vrelo Bosne.
hotelIntro: Sarajevo's valley shape makes location matter. Old-town hotels are best for sightseeing, Ferhadija keeps everything walkable, Marijin Dvor is practical, and Ilidza is quieter but farther from evening old-town life.
rentalCars: Avoid driving in the old centre; rent only for mountain villages, Mostar or longer Bosnia road trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay in Bascarsija for a first visit, especially if you want cafes, cevapi and historic lanes close by.

travelTips.title: Terrain
travelTips.text: Sarajevo rises quickly from the valley floor, so check slopes before booking hillside accommodation with luggage.

travelTips.title: History
travelTips.text: Balance old-town wandering with a museum or guided tour to understand the 1990s siege context respectfully.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Mostar is possible as a long day trip, but it deserves an overnight if your schedule allows.

history.label: Origins
history.text: The name Sarajevo derives from the Turkish noun saray, meaning "palace" or "mansion" (from Persian sarāy, سرای, of the same meaning).
The official name during the 400 years of Ottoman rule was Saraybosna ("Palace of Bosnia"), which remains the city's name in Modern Turkish.
One theory is that the name may have been derived from the Ottoman Turkish term saray ovası, first recorded in 1455, meaning "the plains around the palace" or simply "palace plains".
The first mention of the name Sarajevo was in a 1507 letter written by Firuz Bey.

history.label: Growth
history.text: Scholars disagree on the origin of the evo attached to the end.

history.label: Modern city
history.text: In Slavic languages, the addition of "-evo" may indicate a possessive noun, thereby making the name of Sarajevo 'city of the palace'.
